definition_zh: 点燃；着火；激起（情感、兴趣）；引发（冲突、争论）
definition_en: to start something burning, or to set off a sudden strong reaction such as anger, interest, or conflict
core_image: 火柴头在砂纸上擦出一簇火星，纸角先卷起、再整个烧起来
scene: 实验室里氢气泄漏，一点火星就足以让整间屋子燃起大火。Even a single spark can ignite the gas in the whole room.
sceneCN: 这里 ignite 是「使着火、点燃」（第 1 个义项：使可燃物开始燃烧）；句意：哪怕只有一颗火星，也能让整间屋子的气体燃起来。这个义项最贴近「擦出一簇火星」的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 由基础词加拉丁名词后缀 -io（-ion）构成，义为「点火；点火装置」
由基础词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可燃的；能点着的」
由基础词加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「点火器；点火零件」

senses.title: To set something burning
senses.definition: to make something start to burn
senses.definitionCN: 使某物开始燃烧
senses.example: She struck a match to ignite the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 她划了一根火柴点燃炉子。
senses.why: Ignite goes back to Latin ignis, fire, so the verb names the exact moment when fire begins.
senses.whyCN: ignite 来自拉丁语 ignis（火），因此这个词直接命名「火开始的瞬间」，最贴近核心画面。

senses.title: To catch fire and burn
senses.definition: to start burning by itself, without being lit by a person
senses.definitionCN: 自身开始燃烧，而不是被人点着
senses.example: The dry grass ignited where the spark landed.
senses.exampleCN: 干草在火星落下的地方着了起来。
senses.why: If the verb means to start a fire, the same word can describe the fuel side of the event, the thing that starts burning.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「使火开始」，同一个词也能从燃料的角度说话，即「开始烧起来」，所以成了不及物用法。

senses.title: To excite a strong feeling
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling such as interest, hope, or anger to begin suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 使兴趣、希望或愤怒等强烈情感突然产生
senses.example: The lecture ignited her interest in astronomy.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座点燃了她对天文学的兴趣。
senses.why: A feeling that is sparked in the mind follows the same picture as a flame, a single flash that grows into a blaze.
senses.whyCN: 在心里被擦出的情绪和火焰遵循同一幅画面：一点火星迅速长成大火，所以 ignite 被用来指情感的突然萌发。

senses.title: To set off a conflict or debate
senses.definition: to cause a protest, argument, or violent conflict to start
senses.definitionCN: 使抗议、争执或暴力冲突开始发生
senses.example: The new tax ignited protests across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 新税引发了全国范围的抗议。
senses.why: Conflicts spread from a first spark the way fires do, so reporters say a remark ignited a riot.
senses.whyCN: 冲突像火一样由第一颗火星蔓延开来，所以新闻里说某句话「点燃」了骚乱，引出「引发」的义项。

senses.title: In an engine or burner
senses.definition: of a fuel and air mixture in an engine, to burn at the right moment
senses.definitionCN: 发动机内的燃油与空气混合物在正确时刻燃烧
senses.example: The spark plug must ignite the mixture at exactly the right moment.
senses.exampleCN: 火花塞必须在准确的时刻点燃混合气。
senses.why: Mechanics reuse the fire-starting sense for the controlled little explosion inside a cylinder.
senses.whyCN: 机械师把「点火」的本义借用到气缸内受控的小型燃烧上，于是有了发动机领域的专门用法。

intro.en: Ignite is a learned word built on Latin ignis, fire, and it entered English in the late sixteenth century beside the noun ignition.
intro.cn: ignite 是以拉丁语 ignis（火）为基础的书面词，大约在十六世纪末进入英语，与名词 ignition 几乎同时出现。

items.en: Ignis means fire, and the adjective igneus means fiery.
items.cn: ignis 意为「火」，形容词 igneus 意为「火一样的」。

items.en: The verb ignire means to set on fire, and ignitum is its past participle.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 ignire 意为「点火、使燃烧」，其过去分词形式为 ignitum。

items.en: English speakers borrowed the participle as ignite, to set on fire.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪八十年代借入这个过去分词，形成 ignite，表示「点燃」。

items.en: Chemistry writers use ignite for the moment when matter begins to burn.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪的化学作者用 ignite 描述物质开始燃烧的时刻。

items.en: The engineering sense of igniting fuel in an engine grows with the internal combustion engine.
items.cn: 随着内燃机的出现，十九世纪发展出「在发动机里点燃燃料」的工程义。

items.en: Figurative use spreads widely: remarks ignite debate and songs ignite passion.
items.cn: 现代英语中比喻用法广泛流行：言论「点燃」讨论，歌声「点燃」热情。

note.en: Ignite is the formal word built on the Latin noun for fire; it sits beside the everyday kindle and light, and beside look-alike words such as ignore and ignite-related ignition.
note.cn: ignite 是以拉丁语「火」为基础构成的正式用词，与日常的 kindle、light 相邻；形近词则有 ignore、ignition 等。

entries.definition: the act of starting a fire, or the device that starts an engine
entries.definitionCN: 点火；点火装置（同根名词）

entries.definition: fiery, made of fire
entries.definitionCN: 火一样的（拉丁语形容词，与 ignite 同源）

entries.definition: to pay no attention to someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 忽视；不理会（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自「不知道」的词根）

entries.definition: to start a fire, or to make a feeling begin
to make something start to burn
to cause something to start suddenly

normalIntro.en: Remember ignite through Latin ignis, fire, and through the English family ignition, ignitable, and igniter.
normalIntro.cn: 通过拉丁语 ignis（火）和英语词族 ignition、ignitable、igniter 记住 ignite。

normal.en: Latin ignis, fire, hides inside ignite: the t ending shows a verb was built from it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ignis（火）藏在 ignite 里面，词尾变化说明它被做成了动词。

normal.en: The noun ignition names the act of firing and the car part that fires the fuel.
normal.cn: 名词 ignition 既指「点火」这个动作，也指汽车里给燃料点火的那个部件。

normal.en: Ignite takes an object for the thing set burning: ignite a candle, ignite the fuel.
normal.cn: ignite 后面接被点着的东西：ignite a candle、ignite the fuel。

normal.en: With feelings and events the verb means to start them: ignite interest, ignite debate.
normal.cn: 当宾语是情绪或事件时，这个词表示让它们开始：ignite interest、ignite debate。

normal.en: Compare kindle and light: ignite is the formal, often technical choice in writing about fire and engines.
normal.cn: 对比 kindle 与 light：ignite 更正式，写火与发动机时常用它，技术色彩更强。

abstract.en: See a match head scratching across rough paper and a small orange star jumping off.
abstract.cn: 想象火柴头在粗糙的纸上一划，一颗小小的橙色火星跳出来。

abstract.en: See the flame taking hold on its own, spreading from one dry leaf to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象火焰自己站稳脚跟，从一片枯叶烧到另一片枯叶。

abstract.en: See a single sentence in a classroom lighting up every listener at once.
abstract.cn: 想象课堂上的一句话，让所有听众的眼睛同时亮起来。

examples.en: The engineer explained how the spark plug ignites the fuel.
examples.cn: 工程师解释了火花塞如何点燃燃料。

examples.en: Her first trip abroad ignited a love of foreign languages.
examples.cn: 她的第一次出国旅行点燃了她对语言的热情。

examples.en: The leaked gas could ignite at any moment.
examples.cn: 泄漏的燃气随时可能着火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一哥奈特」——一哥擦亮火柴，点亮了奈特的夜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ignis（火）+ 动词词尾 → 晚期拉丁语 ignire（点火）/ 过去分词 ignitum → 英语 ignite，核心义「让火开始」。

sensesIntro.en: Ignite begins with the physical kindling of fire, extends to a fuel catching fire on its own, then to feelings and conflicts that flare up, and finally to the controlled burning inside an engine.
sensesIntro.cn: ignite 从物理上的「点火」出发，延伸到燃料自行着火，再扩展到突然燃起的情感与冲突，最后落到发动机内受控的燃烧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a match head scratching a spark that starts a fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：火柴头擦出一颗火星，火就烧起来了。

branches.en: The literal sense of lighting a fire is the everyday core.
branches.cn: 字面上的「点火」是日常使用的核心义。

branches.en: The same event seen from the fuel side becomes catching fire.
branches.cn: 同一件事从燃料角度看，就成了「着火」。

branches.en: Feelings and conflicts share the flare-up image of a flame spreading.
branches.cn: 情感与冲突共享「火苗窜起」的画面。

branches.en: Engines copy the fire-starting sense on a small controlled scale.
branches.cn: 发动机把点火义缩小到受控的尺度上使用。

branches.en: All three describe the precise moment when burning begins.
branches.cn: 三个义项都在描述燃烧开始的那一瞬间。

intro.en: Ignite keeps the Latin fire root ign- at its centre, with the English family ignition, igniter, and ignitable around it.
intro.cn: ignite 以拉丁语的火根 ign- 为核心，周围是英语词族 ignition、igniter 与 ignitable。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, ignis is fire, igneus is fiery, and ignire is the verb to set on fire. Its participle ignitum shaped the English verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中 ignis 是火，igneus 是「火一样的」，ignire 是动词「点火」，其分词 ignitum 影响了英语动词的形式。

items.example: The root ign- carries the idea of fire.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ign- 承载「火」的意思。

items.example: Ignis is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: ignis 是整组词背后的名词。

items.example: Ignire gives the verb meaning.
items.exampleCN: ignire 提供了动词义。

items.example: Ignitum is the participle that English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: ignitum 是英语借入的分词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ion turns the verb into ignition.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成名词 ignition。

items.example: The suffix -able forms ignitable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 ignitable。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms igniter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 igniter。

items.example: The prefix re- gives reignite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 构成 reignite。

items.meaning: formed by fire, as of rock
items.example: Igneous rock cooled from molten material.
items.exampleCN: 火成岩由熔融物质冷却而成。

items.example: Ignite keeps the burning sense at its centre.
items.exampleCN: ignite 把「燃烧」的意味留在核心。

definition_zh: 耻辱；不名誉；公开的羞辱；可耻的行为
definition_en: deep public shame that comes from wrongdoing or defeat, or something that brings such shame
core_image: 人被剥去姓名，当众站在那里，所有人都不认识他、也不愿认他
scene: 将军丢了城池，又被逐出军籍，余生都在耻辱中度过。Stripped of his rank and name, the general lived the rest of his life in ignominy.
sceneCN: 这里 ignominy 是「耻辱、不名誉」（第 1 个义项：由过错或失败带来的深切公开羞辱）；句意：被剥夺军衔和姓名之后，这位将军余生都活在耻辱之中。

pos.zh: 耻辱；不名誉；公开羞辱；可耻行为

derivatives.zh: 由名词 ignominy 加后缀 -ious 构成，义为「可耻的；不光彩的」
由形容词 ignominious 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可耻地；丢脸地」
由否定前缀 in-（不）+ nobilis（显赫的）构成，义为「卑劣的；不光彩的」，与 ignominy 共享否定前缀

senses.title: Deep public shame
senses.definition: a state of deep shame caused by wrongdoing or great failure and felt before other people
senses.definitionCN: 因过错或重大失败而在众人面前感到的深切羞耻
senses.example: The minister resigned in disgrace and lived the rest of his life in ignominy.
senses.exampleCN: 那位部长耻辱地辞职，余生都在不名誉中度过。
senses.why: Latin in- means not and nomen means name, so ignominy is literally a loss of good name, and a damaged name is what shame feels like.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中 in- 表「不」、nomen 表「名字」，ignominy 字面就是「失去好名声」，而名声受损正是耻辱的切身感受。

senses.title: A shameful act or outcome
senses.definition: an action or result that deserves contempt and brings shame to those involved
senses.definitionCN: 值得鄙视、给当事人带来羞耻的行为或结果
senses.example: Destroying the letters was the greatest ignominy of that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 烧掉那些信件是那个冬天最丢脸的一件事。
senses.why: If a lost name is the image, the thing that costs a person their name can itself be called an ignominy.
senses.whyCN: 既然画面是「丢掉名声」，那么让人丢掉名声的那件事本身也可以叫 ignominy，由状态义转成事件义。

senses.title: Defeat that strips honour
senses.definition: a defeat so total that the losers are treated with contempt
senses.definitionCN: 彻底到使败者被人轻视的失败
senses.example: The army retreated in ignominy after the siege collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 围城瓦解之后，军队屈辱地撤退了。
senses.why: A defeat removes the honour that a good name stands for, so losing badly is experienced as a loss of name.
senses.whyCN: 战败会剥夺好名声所代表的荣誉，所以惨败被体验成「丢了名字」，这就是屈辱的失败这一义项。

senses.title: Rebuke or punishment that shames
senses.definition: a rebuke or penalty whose main point is to make the person appear contemptible
senses.definitionCN: 以使人显得可鄙为主要目的的斥责或处罚
senses.example: He was dismissed before the whole staff, an ignominy he never forgot.
senses.exampleCN: 他当着一整班员工的面被解职，这种当众羞辱他一辈子都忘不了。
senses.why: The name is removed in front of witnesses, so the word also names the public act that performs the removal.
senses.whyCN: 名字是在众人面前被摘掉的，所以这个词也指「当众摘掉名字」的那个动作，即羞辱性的责罚。

intro.en: Ignominy comes through Old French and Latin from in-, not, plus nomen, name: literally a loss of name, hence dishonour.
intro.cn: ignominy 经由古法语与拉丁语而来，由 in-（不）+ nomen（名字）构成，字面意思是「失去名字」，引申为「不名誉」。

items.en: Nomen means name, and the privative prefix in- means not.
items.cn: nomen 意为「名字」，否定的前缀 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Ignominia means loss of name, disgrace, or dishonour.
items.cn: ignominia 意为「失去名字、蒙羞、不名誉」。

items.en: Ignominie keeps the Latin form in medieval French and passes it to English.
items.cn: 中世纪法语保留 ignominie 这一形式，并把它传给英语。

items.en: The noun enters English as ignominy, naming public disgrace.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后 ignominy 进入英语，表示公开的耻辱。

items.en: The adjective ignominious grows out of the noun and is now the commoner form.
items.cn: 十七世纪由名词派生出形容词 ignominious，如今它的使用频率更高。

items.en: Today ignominy is a literary and journalistic word, often used for political or military downfall.
items.cn: 现代英语中 ignominy 是文学与新闻用词，常用于政治或军事上的垮台。

note.en: Ignominy is a formal noun for lost name and public shame; its look-alikes share the Latin name root, while its near meanings range from everyday shame to dishonour.
note.cn: ignominy 是表示「失去名声、公开蒙羞」的正式名词；形近词共享拉丁语「名字」词根，近义词则从日常的羞耻到名誉上的失格都有。

entries.definition: deserving shame and contempt
entries.definitionCN: 可耻的；不光彩的（同根形容词）

entries.definition: not honourable, of low character
entries.definitionCN: 卑劣的；不光彩的（与 ignominy 共享否定前缀 in-）

entries.definition: existing in name only
entries.definitionCN: 名义上的（同含拉丁语「名字」词根 nomen，但与 ignominy 只是同根）

entries.definition: the loss of respect from other people
a painful feeling of having done wrong
a loss of honour or good reputation

normalIntro.en: Build ignominy from its two Latin parts: in-, not, and nomen, name, plus the English family ignominious, ignominiously, and ignoble.
normalIntro.cn: 用两个拉丁语部件记住 ignominy：in-（不）+ nomen（名字），再加上英语词族 ignominious、ignominiously、ignoble。

normal.en: Latin nomen, name, hides in the middle of ignominy.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nomen（名字）藏在 ignominy 中间。

normal.en: The prefix in- denies it: no name, no good reputation.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 表示否定：没有名字，就没有好名声。

normal.en: The adjective is ignominious and the adverb ignominiously, both commoner than the noun today.
normal.cn: 形容词是 ignominious，副词是 ignominiously，如今都比名词更常用。

normal.en: The noun takes prepositions of state and journey: in ignominy, end in ignominy, retreat in ignominy.
normal.cn: 这个名词常跟状态与走向的搭配：in ignominy、end in ignominy、retreat in ignominy。

normal.en: Compare disgrace: disgrace is everyday, ignominy is formal and marked as literary.
normal.cn: 对比 disgrace：disgrace 更日常，ignominy 正式，带有文学色彩。

abstract.en: See a name being rubbed off a brass plate until only a blank mark is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字从铜牌上被磨掉，最后只剩一块空白。

abstract.en: See a crowd turning its back on one person standing alone in the square.
abstract.cn: 想象广场上只剩一个人站着，人群纷纷转过身去。

abstract.en: See a defeated flag folded without ceremony and thrown into a box.
abstract.cn: 想象一面战败的旗子没有仪式地被叠起，扔进箱子里。

examples.en: The scandal brought years of ignominy to the family.
examples.cn: 那桩丑闻让这个家族多年蒙受耻辱。

examples.en: He preferred exile to the ignominy of a public trial.
examples.cn: 他宁愿流亡，也不愿承受公开审判带来的羞辱。

examples.en: The company ended its most ambitious project in ignominy.
examples.cn: 这家公司最宏大的项目以耻辱收场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个糯米泥」——被人一个糯米团子似的揉捏、糊在脸上，当众丢尽脸面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ nomen（名字）→ ignominia（失去名字；耻辱）→ 古法语 ignominie → 英语 ignominy，核心义「失去好名声」。

sensesIntro.en: Ignominy starts as the state of having lost a good name, widens to the act or result that costs someone that name, and then to humiliating defeat and to punishment that shames in public.
sensesIntro.cn: ignominy 起初指「失去好名声」的状态，扩展到使人失去名声的行为或结果，再进一步指屈辱的失败和让人当众蒙羞的责罚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing before everyone with the name removed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人当着众人的面被抹去了名字。

branches.en: The state of deep public shame is the central sense.
branches.cn: 深切的公开羞耻是核心义项。

branches.en: The shameful act or result is the event sense.
branches.cn: 可耻的行为或结果是事件义项。

branches.en: A defeat that strips honour extends the lost-name image to battle and sport.
branches.cn: 剥夺荣誉的失败把「丢了名字」的画面扩展到战场与赛场。

branches.en: A shaming rebuke is the active, performed sense.
branches.cn: 羞辱性的斥责是「主动施加」的义项。

branches.en: All three present a person losing the good name others used to know.
branches.cn: 三个义项都呈现一个人失去别人熟悉的好名声。

intro.en: Ignominy is built from the Latin negating prefix in- plus the noun nomen, with English ignominious and ignoble keeping the same shape.
intro.cn: ignominy 由拉丁语否定前缀 in- 加名词 nomen 构成，英语的 ignominious、ignoble 保留了同样的结构。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, nomen is name and in- or ig- before n negates it, giving ignominia, a name taken away and so dishonour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中 nomen 是「名字」，in- 在 n 前写作 ig- 表示否定，合成 ignominia，即「名字被拿走」，也就是不名誉。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the noun after it.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定后面的名词。

items.meaningCN: 在 n 前的否定前缀形式
items.example: The prefix takes the form ign- before nomen.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在 nomen 前写作 ign-。

items.example: Nomen supplies the meaning of name.
items.exampleCN: nomen 提供「名字」的词义。

items.example: Ignominia is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: ignominia 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the English noun ignominy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成英语名词 ignominy。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ious forms ignominious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ious 构成 ignominious。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms ignominiously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 ignominiously。

items.meaningCN: 以 y 结尾名词的复数词尾
items.example: The plural ending gives ignominies.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾给出 ignominies。

items.example: Ignoble uses the same negating prefix.
items.exampleCN: ignoble 使用了同一个否定前缀。

definition_zh: 难以辨认的；字迹潦草的；印刷模糊的
definition_en: too unclear to be read, because the handwriting is messy or the letters are faint or damaged
core_image: 纸上密密麻麻的笔画挤成一团，眼睛知道那是字，却怎么也读不出来
scene: 老医生开的处方字迹潦草，药剂师盯着看了半天也读不出来。The pharmacists stared at the prescription, but the handwriting was illegible.
sceneCN: 这里 illegible 是「难以辨认的」（第 1 个义项：字迹太乱或字母太淡，读不出来）；句意：药剂师盯着处方看，可那字迹根本认不出。

pos.zh: 难以辨认的；字迹潦草的；模糊不清的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 illegible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「难以辨认地；潦草地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「难以辨认；字迹不清」
去掉否定前缀 il- 后的肯定形式，义为「清晰易读的」

senses.title: Handwriting that cannot be read
senses.definition: of handwriting, too untidy or unclear for the letters to be recognised
senses.definitionCN: 手写字太乱或太模糊，辨认不出字母
senses.example: His notes were so illegible that nobody could copy them.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笔记太难认，没人能抄。
senses.why: Latin legere means to read, and the negative prefix makes the word say not readable, with the core image of strokes clotted together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 legere 意为「读」，否定前缀使这个词意为「读不出来」，正对应笔画挤成一团的核心画面。

senses.title: Print too faint or damaged to read
senses.definition: of printed or written text, faded, smudged, or damaged so that the words cannot be made out
senses.definitionCN: 印刷或写下的文字褪色、污损或残缺，无法辨认
senses.example: The labels on the old jars had faded until they were illegible.
senses.exampleCN: 旧罐子上的标签褪色得几乎认不出来了。
senses.why: The same unreadable state can come from outside the hand, through fading ink, water damage, or a faint photocopy.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「读不出」状态也可能来自字迹之外，比如墨色褪去、受潮或被复印得太淡，于是这个词也用于印刷与物品标识。

senses.title: A signature or written mark no one can identify
senses.definition: of a signature or set of letters, written so loosely that the name or word cannot be identified at all
senses.definitionCN: 签名或字串写得过于随意，根本认不出是谁的名字或哪个词
senses.example: An illegible signature ran along the bottom of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 合同底部的一个签名龙飞凤舞，认不出是谁。
senses.why: A signature loses its purpose when it cannot be read as a name, which is why the word is so often applied to them.
senses.whyCN: 签名一旦读不出名字就失去了作用，所以这个词经常被用在签名上，成为常见义项。

senses.title: In law, not clear enough to be official
senses.definition: in legal and formal writing, described of a document or clause that cannot be read clearly enough to be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与正式文书中，文件或条款字迹不清，无法据此执行
senses.example: The court set aside the will because one crucial page was illegible.
senses.exampleCN: 因为关键的一页看不清，法院撤销了这份遗嘱。
senses.why: When a document controls money or rights, a text that cannot be read becomes a formal defect, so the word takes on a legal use.
senses.whyCN: 当文件决定财产与权利时，「读不出」就变成了形式上的瑕疵，于是这个词有了法律上的专门用法。

intro.en: Illegible is built from Latin legere, to read, with the negative prefix in-, which changes to il- before l.
intro.cn: illegible 由拉丁语 legere（读）加否定前缀 in- 构成，in- 在 l 前写作 il-。

items.en: Legere means to read or gather, and legibilis means that can be read.
items.cn: legere 意为「读、采集」，legibilis 意为「可读的」。

items.en: The negated form illegibilis marks a text that cannot be read.
items.cn: 否定形式 illegibilis 表示「读不出来的文字」。

items.en: The positive legible arrives first, from Old French and Latin, as a word for what can be read.
items.cn: 先进入英语的是肯定形式 legible，来自古法语与拉丁语，表示「能读的」。

items.en: The negated illegible appears and spreads as printing expands.
items.cn: 随着印刷业的发展，否定形式 illegible 在十七世纪出现并流行。

items.en: Illegible is applied to handwriting, stamps, and legal documents.
items.cn: 十九世纪把 illegible 用于手写、印章和法律文书。

items.en: Digital use adds illegible scans and illegible screenshots.
items.cn: 现代英语中又出现 illegible scans、illegible screenshots 等数字语境用法。

note.en: Illegible sits beside its positive pair legible and the suffix -ible, and near meaning words such as unreadable and scribbled.
note.cn: illegible 与肯定形式 legible 及后缀 -ible 成对，近义一侧则有 unreadable、scribbled 等词。

entries.definition: clear enough to read easily
entries.definitionCN: 清晰易读的（illegible 的肯定形式）

entries.definition: not allowed by law
entries.definitionCN: 非法的（同用 il- 否定前缀，但词根是「法律」lex，与「读」无关）

entries.definition: allowed or suitable to be chosen
entries.definitionCN: 有资格的；合适的（只是拼写相近，词源来自「挑选」，与 illegible 不同）

entries.definition: impossible or unpleasant to read
entries.definitionCN: 读不出的；读起来无趣的

entries.definition: impossible to understand or decode
entries.definitionCN: 无法解读的；破译不了的

entries.definition: written quickly and untidily

normalIntro.en: Build illegible from Latin legere, to read, with the negative prefix il- and the suffix -ible, and remember it against legible.
normalIntro.cn: 用拉丁语 legere（读）加否定前缀 il- 与后缀 -ible 构成 illegible，并与 legible 对照记忆。

normal.en: Latin legere, to read, is the same root as legend and lecture.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 legere（读）也是 legend 与 lecture 的词根。

normal.en: The prefix in- becomes il- before l to avoid awkward doubling.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 在 l 前变成 il-，以免两个 l 连在一起拗口。

normal.en: Drop the prefix and the word flips: legible is clear, illegible is hopeless.
normal.cn: 去掉前缀意思就翻转：legible 清晰可读，illegible 根本读不出。

normal.en: The suffix -ible marks a possibility, so illegible means it cannot be read.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ible 表示「能够」，因此 illegible 意为「读不出来」。

normal.en: The noun is illegibility and the adverb is illegibly when describing notes and labels.
normal.cn: 名词是 illegibility，副词是 illegibly，用来描述笔记和标签。

abstract.en: See a doctor scribbling a prescription while a pharmacist squints at it.
abstract.cn: 想象医生潦草地开着处方，药剂师眯着眼使劲看。

abstract.en: See old labels under a dusty jar, the letters eaten away by sun.
abstract.cn: 想象落满灰尘的罐子下压着旧标签，字母被日晒吃掉了。

abstract.en: See a signature that looks like a single long loop.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名长得像一条长长的圈套，看不出是谁。

examples.en: The letter was so illegible that we had to guess half the words.
examples.cn: 那封信太潦草，有一半的词只能靠猜。

examples.en: Please write clearly, as the scan is often illegible.
examples.cn: 请写清楚些，因为扫描件常常看不清。

examples.en: Time had made the ink faint and the names almost illegible.
examples.cn: 时间让墨迹变淡，那些名字几乎认不出来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿了识不出」——饿得眼花，字都认不出来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 legere（读）→ legibilis（可读的）→ 否定形式 in- + legibilis，in- 在 l 前写作 il- → 英语 illegible，核心义「读不出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Illegible begins with messy handwriting, extends to any faint or damaged print, then to signatures that hide a name, and finally to documents whose unclear text has legal consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: illegible 从潦草的手写出发，扩展到一切模糊或破损的印刷文字，再指认不出名字的签名，最后落到文字不清会产生法律后果的文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strokes clotted into a mass that the eye cannot turn into words.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔画挤成一团，眼睛无法把它们读成文字。

branches.en: Messy handwriting is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 潦草的手写是日常义项。

branches.en: Faint or damaged print broadens the cause of being unreadable.
branches.cn: 模糊或破损的印刷让「读不出」的原因更广。

branches.en: An unreadable signature is a name that cannot be recovered.
branches.cn: 认不出的签名就是找不回来的名字。

branches.en: In law, unclear text turns into a formal problem.
branches.cn: 在法律里，文字不清会变成形式上的问题。

branches.en: All three describe letters the eye cannot decode.
branches.cn: 三个义项都描述眼睛无法辨认的字母。

intro.en: Illegible joins the negative prefix il- to the Latin reading root leg- and the suffix -ible, with legible, illegibly, and illegibility around it.
intro.cn: illegible 由否定前缀 il-、拉丁语「读」词根 leg- 与后缀 -ible 组成，周围有 legible、illegibly、illegibility。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere means to read, legibilis means readable, and the negated illegibilis means that cannot be read.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为「读」，legibilis 意为「可读的」，否定形式 illegibilis 意为「读不出来的」。

items.example: The prefix il- negates the word that follows.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 il- 否定后面的词。

items.example: The root leg- carries the act of reading.
items.exampleCN: 词根 leg- 承载「读」的动作。

items.example: Legere is the verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: legere 是整组词背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms legible and illegible.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 legible 与 illegible。

items.example: Legible is the positive partner of illegible.
items.exampleCN: legible 是 illegible 的肯定对应词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms illegibly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 illegibly。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms illegibility.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 illegibility。

items.example: Legend shares the same reading root.
items.exampleCN: legend 共享同一个「读」词根。

items.meaning: the state of being against the law
items.example: Illegality builds on the law root lex instead.
items.exampleCN: illegality 用的是「法律」词根 lex，与「读」无关。

definition_zh: 照亮；照明；阐明；启发；(用彩灯)装饰
definition_en: to light up a place, to make something clear, or to decorate something with lights
core_image: 昏黑的房间里有人擦亮一根火柴，墙上的形状忽然显现出来
scene: 夜里停电，走廊一片漆黑，父亲举着一盏油灯慢慢走过。The oil lamp on the sill illuminates the narrow hallway until morning.
sceneCN: 这里 illuminate 是「照亮」（第 1 个义项：给地方提供光亮）；句意：窗台上那盏油灯一直照着狭窄的走廊，直到天亮。这正是核心画面中「光一出现，黑暗里的东西便显形」的那一步。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加后缀 -tion 构成，义为「照明；照明设备；启发」
由动词加后缀 -ing 构成，义为「富有启发的；照亮用的」
由动词加后缀 -ant 构成，义为「光源；发光体」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「被照亮的；带彩饰插图的」

senses.title: To give light to a place
senses.definition: to supply light to a place or object so that it becomes bright
senses.definitionCN: 向某地或某物提供光线，使其明亮
senses.example: Floodlights illuminate the stadium during the evening match.
senses.exampleCN: 晚场比赛时，泛光灯照亮了整座体育场。
senses.why: Latin lumen means light, and the in- prefix here intensifies it, so the verb is literally to put light into something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lumen 意为「光」，前缀 in- 在这里起加强作用，所以这个动词字面上就是「把光放进去」，照亮一个地方。

senses.title: To make a subject clear
senses.definition: to explain something so that it becomes easier to understand
senses.definitionCN: 解释某事，使其更容易被理解
senses.example: The new evidence illuminates why the plan failed.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据清楚说明了计划失败的原因。
senses.why: Light making dark shapes visible is the same process as explanation making a problem visible to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 光让黑暗中的形状显现，解释则让问题在头脑中显现，两者是同一个过程，所以「照亮」延伸为「阐明」。

senses.title: To help someone understand
senses.definition: to give someone insight, especially through a teacher, a book, or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过师长、书籍或某个想法给人以洞察和领悟
senses.example: Her lectures illuminated a whole generation of students.
senses.exampleCN: 她的讲座启发了一整代学生。
senses.why: If light makes the eye able to see, the same word can describe whatever opens the mind to see clearly.
senses.whyCN: 既然光让眼睛看得见，同一个词也可以描述让头脑看清的东西，因此「照亮」长出「启发」义。

senses.title: To decorate with lights
senses.definition: to decorate a building, street, or object with bright lights
senses.definitionCN: 用明亮灯饰装饰建筑物、街道或物件
senses.example: Every winter the council illuminates the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 每到冬天，市政会把那座老桥装点得灯火通明。
senses.why: Festival practise put many lights into one place, so the verb moved from lighting a spot to decorating with lights.
senses.whyCN: 节庆习俗把许多灯集中到同一处，动词于是从「照亮一处」滑向「用灯装饰」。

senses.title: To brighten the face or mood
senses.definition: to make a person or feeling brighter, as if lit from within
senses.definitionCN: 使人或情绪焕发光彩，仿佛被从内点亮
senses.example: Good news illuminated her tired face.
senses.exampleCN: 好消息让她疲惫的脸上焕发光彩。
senses.why: A lit object looks brighter, and people use the same image for faces and moods that suddenly brighten.
senses.whyCN: 被照亮的东西看起来更亮，人们便用同一意象形容突然变亮的脸和心情。

senses.title: To produce light itself
senses.definition: to shine with light of its own, as a lamp or a screen does
senses.definitionCN: 像灯或屏幕那样自身发出光亮
senses.example: The dial illuminates in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 表盘在黑暗中会自己发光。
senses.why: When the source rather than the target of light is the subject, the verb shifts from lighting up a place to shine by itself.
senses.whyCN: 当句子的主体由「被照的地方」换成「光源」时，这个动词就从「照亮某处」变成「自身发光」。

senses.title: To decorate a manuscript
senses.definition: to decorate a handwritten book with gold, colours, or pictures called illuminations
senses.definitionCN: 用手抄本彩画为手写书籍作装饰，这种彩饰称为 illumination
senses.example: Monks illuminated the pages with gold leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们用金箔为书页作彩饰。
senses.why: In historical use, bright colours and gold were laid onto the page like light, so to light up meant to add painted decoration.
senses.whyCN: 在历史用法中，亮色与金色被点染在书页上，好像给纸面加了光，于是「加光」就是给手抄本加彩画。

intro.en: Illuminate comes from Latin illuminare, to light up, built on lumen, light, and passed through Middle English as a bookish word.
intro.cn: illuminate 来自拉丁语 illuminare（照亮），词根是 lumen（光），经中古英语进入英语，最初是文人用词。

items.en: Lumen means light, and illuminare means to light up or brighten.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lumen 意为「光」，illuminare 意为「照亮、使明亮」。

items.en: Church Latin uses illuminare for divine enlightenment and for decorated manuscripts.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，illuminare 既指神圣的「启示」，也指给手抄本加彩饰。

items.en: The verb past participle illumine passes into French as a literary word.
items.cn: 该动词的法语形式 illumine 以文学用语的身份进入古法语。

items.en: The word enters English as a learned term for lighting and for understanding.
items.cn: 这个词以书面语身份进入中古英语，既指照明，也指理解。

items.en: Writers borrow the full Latin verb illuminate and give it the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪作家借入拉丁语原形 illuminate，并定下了现代拼写。

items.en: Illumination now covers lighting, decoration, insight, and even ancient manuscripts.
items.cn: 现代英语中，illumination 涵盖照明、装饰、启发，甚至古代手抄本的彩饰。

note.en: Illuminate sits next to the Latin lumen family and to the everyday words for light and for explaining.
note.cn: illuminate 与拉丁语 lumen「光」词族相邻，也与日常表示「照亮」和「解释」的词义场相通。

entries.definition: light, or the act of lighting something up
giving useful insight
giving off light, especially in the dark
an expert or famous person who inspires others
entries.definitionCN: 杰出人物；启迪他人的名人

entries.definition: the source of light that makes a scene bright
to become bright or to make bright
to make lighter or happier
to make something easier to understand
to explain an idea clearly

normalIntro.en: Break illuminate into in- plus lumen, light, and you get to put light into: a room, a problem, or a face.
normalIntro.cn: 把 illuminate 拆成 in- 加 lumen「光」，就是「把光放进去」：放进房间、放进问题、放上脸。

normal.en: Latin lumen means light, so illuminate literally means to put light in.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lumen 意为「光」，所以 illuminate 字面就是「把光放进去」。

normal.en: Illuminate is not a word, and illumination is the noun.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：正确形式是 illuminate，名词是 illumination。

normal.en: The adjective illuminating describes explanations that make matters clear.
normal.cn: 形容词 illuminating 形容能把事情讲清楚的解释。

normal.en: Luminous and luminary share the same light root.
normal.cn: luminous 与 luminary 共享同一个「光」词根。

normal.en: The in- prefix tells you the light goes into something, and the ending -ate makes it a verb.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 告诉你光进入某物之中，词尾 -ate 让它成为动词。

abstract.en: Picture a match being struck in a dark room and the shapes on the wall appearing.
abstract.cn: 想象在漆黑的房间里划亮一根火柴，墙上的形状随即显现。

abstract.en: Think of a torch beam moving down a dark corridor until the door plate can be read.
abstract.cn: 想象手电光束沿暗走廊移动，直到看得清门牌。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher switching on a projector, and the whole lesson suddenly makes sense.
abstract.cn: 想象老师打开投影仪，整堂课忽然都说得通了。

examples.en: Candles illuminated the old chapel on the evening of the wedding.
examples.cn: 婚礼当晚，烛光照亮了古老的礼拜堂。

examples.en: The report illuminates the reasons behind the falling birth rate.
examples.cn: 这份报告阐明了出生率下降的原因。

examples.en: A powerful lamp illuminates the whole shelter during the night.
examples.cn: 夜里，一盏强光灯照亮了整个庇护所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一路明内特」——一路明晃晃地走进去，黑暗里顿时亮堂起来；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lumen「光」→ illuminare（使有光、照亮）→ 英语 illuminate，核心义「把光放进去」。同根的 luminous、luminary 如今表示「发光的」「杰出人物」。

sensesIntro.en: Illuminate begins with physical light in a place, then light as understanding in the mind, then light as decoration and as a brightness of face or mood.
sensesIntro.cn: illuminate 先指给地方带来物理的光，再指给头脑带来理解的光，最后指用灯装饰以及脸上或心情忽然变亮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp is brought into a dark room and everything in it becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人把灯拿进漆黑的房间，房间里的一切随之显形。

branches.en: Physical lighting is the original and most common sense.
branches.cn: 物理意义上的照明是最原始、最常用的义项。

branches.en: Light for the mind gives explanation and inspiration.
branches.cn: 照进头脑的光，长出阐明与启发两个义项。

branches.en: Festive and manuscript decoration is light turned into ornament.
branches.cn: 节庆彩灯与手抄本彩饰都是把光变成装饰。

branches.en: A lit face is the physical brightness carried over to feeling.
branches.cn: 发亮的脸是把物理的亮迁移到情绪上。

branches.en: When the lamp itself is the subject, lighting becomes shining.
branches.cn: 句子主语变成灯本身时，「照亮」就变成了「发光」。

intro.en: Illuminate is built on Latin lumen, light, with the in- prefix and the Latin verb ending; English adds illumination, illuminating, and illuminant.
intro.cn: illuminate 由拉丁语 lumen「光」带着 in- 前缀和动词词尾构成；英语又在它周围造出 illumination、illuminating 与 illuminant。

latinIntro.en: Latin lumen is the light root, and illuminare is the verb that puts light into something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lumen 是表示「光」的词根，illuminare 是「给某物加上光」的动词。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of light going into a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「光进入某处」的意思。

items.example: Lumen is the light root of the word family.
items.exampleCN: lumen 是这个词族的「光」词根。

items.example: Illuminare is the direct source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: illuminare 是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: The ending -ate marks the word as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 表明它是一个动词。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms illumination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 illumination。

items.example: Illumination names both the light and the insight.
items.exampleCN: illumination 既指光，也指启发。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms illuminating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 illuminating。

items.example: Illuminating describes a clear explanation.
items.exampleCN: illuminating 形容清楚的解释。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表执行者或事物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant forms illuminant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 illuminant。

items.example: Illuminant names the light source itself.
items.exampleCN: illuminant 指光源本身。

definition_zh: 错觉；幻觉；假象；幻想；错误的观念
definition_en: a false idea, or something that looks real to the eye but is not
core_image: 沙漠尽头浮动着一片湖面，走近却只剩滚烫的沙
scene: 舞台上灯光很暗，观众看见魔术师把一枚硬币悬在半空。From the back row it looked like pure illusion.
sceneCN: 这里 illusion 是「错觉、假象」（第 1 个义项：眼睛看到的东西其实并不真实）；句意：坐在后排看去，那纯粹是错觉。它和核心画面一样：眼睛笃定看到了，东西却并不在那里。

derivatives.zh: 源自拉丁 illusorius，义为「虚幻的；不实的」
由词干加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「迷惑人的；虚幻的」
由名词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「魔术师；幻想者」
由前缀 dis- 加 illusion 构成，义为「使醒悟；使不再抱幻想」

senses.title: Something that looks real but is not
senses.definition: a false impression given by the way things look or sound
senses.definitionCN: 由事物的外观或声音造成的错误印象
senses.example: The mirage is a familiar illusion on hot desert roads.
senses.exampleCN: 在炎热的沙漠公路上，海市蜃楼是一种常见的错觉。
senses.why: Latin ludere means to play, and in- means against, so an illusion is something the eye is played with, a picture that is not the thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ludere 意为「玩弄」，in- 表示「朝向」，所以 illusion 就是被「戏弄」出的画面：眼睛看到的并不是实物。

senses.title: A false belief about reality
senses.definition: a belief that is not true, often one that a person wants to keep
senses.definitionCN: 一种不真实的看法，往往是人们愿意继续相信的看法
senses.example: He was under the illusion that the money would last forever.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直误以为这笔钱永远花不完。
senses.why: The same word moves from the eye to the mind: what the eye is tricked into seeing, the mind can be tricked into believing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从眼睛挪到头脑：眼睛会被骗着看见，头脑也会被骗着相信。

senses.title: A false impression of ease or control
senses.definition: a feeling that something is easier or safer than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某事比实际更容易或更安全的错误感觉
senses.example: The calm sea gave an illusion of safety.
senses.exampleCN: 平静的海面给人安全的假象。
senses.why: When an outer appearance is too smooth, it hides the danger behind it, and the word names that smooth surface.
senses.whyCN: 当外在表象过于平稳时，它会掩盖背后的危险，这个词命名的就是那层平稳的表皮。

senses.title: A trick performed by a magician
senses.definition: a performance in which objects seem to appear, vanish, or float
senses.definitionCN: 让物体看起来出现、消失或漂浮的表演
senses.example: The magician finished with an illusion involving three glass boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 魔术师最后表演了一个涉及三个玻璃箱的戏法。
senses.why: The stage artist deliberately plays with the eye, which is exactly what ludere suggests, so the trick itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 舞台艺人有意「玩弄」观众的眼睛，正合 ludere 的本义，于是戏法本身也用了这个名字。

senses.title: A deceptive visual pattern
senses.definition: a picture designed so that the eye reports something the brain knows is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 一种刻意设计的图样，让眼睛报出头脑明知不对的信息
senses.example: In the illusion two lines of equal length look unequal.
senses.exampleCN: 在这张视错觉图里，两条一样长的线看起来却不一样长。
senses.why: Optical patterns make the play of the eye visible and measurable, so the trick becomes a study object.
senses.whyCN: 光学图样让眼睛受到的戏弄变得可见、可测量，戏法因此变成了研究对象。

senses.title: Something nonexistent treated as real
senses.definition: a thing that only seems to exist and has no real substance
senses.definitionCN: 只是看起来存在、没有真实实体的事物
senses.example: Wealth built on nothing may prove to be an illusion.
senses.exampleCN: 建立在虚空之上的财富，到头来也许只是虚幻。
senses.why: If the eye can be played with, then what it reports can be dismissed as unreal, and a whole object becomes illusory.
senses.whyCN: 既然眼睛能被戏弄，它报告的东西就可以被判定为不真实，于是整整一个事物都可能只是虚幻。

intro.en: Illusion comes from Latin illusionem, a mocking or a deception, from illudere, to play with or mock, and enters English through Old French.
intro.cn: illusion 来自拉丁语 illusionem（嘲弄、欺骗），源于动词 illudere（玩弄、戏弄），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Ludere means to play, and inludere or illudere means to play upon or mock.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为「玩」，inludere 或 illudere 意为「玩弄、戏弄」。

items.en: The noun illusio means a mocking or a deceiving of the senses or the mind.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语名词 illusio 意为嘲弄，或对感官与头脑的欺骗。

items.en: The French form illusion carries the sense of a deceptive appearance.
items.cn: 古法语形式 illusion 带有「骗人的外表」之意。

items.en: The word enters English first as a term for deception and mocking.
items.cn: 十四世纪该词进入英语，最初指欺骗与嘲弄。

items.en: Scientists begin to use it for optical and physical tricks of the eye.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，科学家用它指光学与物理上的视觉把戏。

items.en: Literature and psychology extend illusion to wishful and false beliefs.
items.cn: 现代英语中，文学与心理学把这个词扩展到一厢情愿的错误信念。

note.en: Illusion belongs to the Latin ludere, play, family and sits beside everyday words for wrong beliefs and deceptive looks.
note.cn: illusion 属于拉丁语 ludere「玩」词族，并与日常表示「错误信念」和「骗人外表」的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: not real, even though it seems to be
deceptive, likely to mislead
a person who performs magic tricks
to free someone from a pleasant but false belief
a firm belief that is false; the letters are easy to confuse with illusion
entries.definitionCN: 妄想；错误信念，只是拼写与 illusion 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an image of water in the desert that is not really there
a pleasing picture in the imagination
a wrong idea that people believe

normalIntro.en: Illusion is i plus ludere, play, played against your eye: the picture is a trick, and the trick, not the thing, is what you get.
normalIntro.cn: illusion 就是 in- 加 ludere「玩」作用于你的眼睛：画面是一场把戏，你拿到的只有把戏，没有实物。

normal.en: Latin ludere means to play, the same root that appears in ludicrous.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为「玩」，ludicrous 里也藏着这个词根。

normal.en: An optical illusion plays with the eye, while an optical lens corrects it.
normal.cn: optical illusion 是在玩弄眼睛，而镜片是在修正眼睛。

normal.en: Be under the illusion that means to believe something untrue.
normal.cn: be under the illusion that 表示「误以为某事是真的」。

normal.en: To dispel an illusion is to clear it away the way fog is cleared from a window.
normal.cn: dispel an illusion 就是把幻想像窗上的雾一样抹掉。

normal.en: Illusory is the adjective for what illusion produces.
normal.cn: illusory 是形容 illusion 所产生之物「虚幻」的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture water shining at the end of a hot road, which turns into dry sand as you walk closer.
abstract.cn: 想象炎热公路尽头的一片水光，走近才发现只是干沙。

abstract.en: Think of two parallel lines that seem to bend the moment arrows are added to their ends.
abstract.cn: 想象两条平行线，两端添上箭头后看起来竟弯曲了。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with a beautiful smooth border that conceals a deep drop inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图边界平滑漂亮，里面却藏着深坑。

examples.en: The mirror creates the illusion of a larger room.
examples.cn: 这面镜子营造出房间更大的错觉。

examples.en: Do not labour under the illusion that tax will stay the same.
examples.cn: 别误以为税率会保持不变。

examples.en: Children often cherish the illusion that adults never fear anything.
examples.cn: 孩子们常常幻想着大人从不会害怕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一路寻」——一路上追寻的东西，到头来只是虚影；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ludere「玩、戏耍」→ illudere（戏弄）→ illusionem（嘲弄、欺骗）→ 古法语 illusion → 英语 illusion，核心义「被眼睛或头脑玩弄出的画面」。同族的 illusory、disillusion 都带「假」与「戳破假」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: Illusion starts as a trick played on the eye, spreads to a false belief in the mind, and ends up naming pure unreality.
sensesIntro.cn: illusion 从眼睛受骗的画面出发，扩展到头脑相信的假观念，最后指纯粹不真实之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lake glitters at the far end of a desert, but walking there finds only hot sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙漠尽头波光粼粼的一片湖，走到眼前却只剩滚烫的沙。

branches.en: The false picture shown to the eye is the first sense.
branches.cn: 眼睛收到的假画面是第一个义项。

branches.en: The same deception moves from sight to belief.
branches.cn: 同一种欺骗从视觉转移到信念上。

branches.en: A smooth appearance of safety and a designed visual pattern are both staged deceptions.
branches.cn: 平稳的表面安全感与精心设计的视错觉图，都是刻意安排的欺骗。

branches.en: A stage trick is the deliberate version of the everyday illusion.
branches.cn: 魔术戏法是日常错觉的刻意版本。

branches.en: What the eye is played with can be declared to have no substance at all.
branches.cn: 被眼睛戏弄出来的东西，可以被判定为根本没有实体。

intro.en: Illusion is built on Latin ludere, to play, with the in- prefix and the Latin noun ending -io; English adds illusory, illusive, and disillusion.
intro.cn: illusion 由拉丁语 ludere「玩」加 in- 前缀和名词词尾 -io 构成；英语又衍生出 illusory、illusive 与 disillusion。

latinIntro.en: Latin ludere means to play, and illudere means to play upon, which is to deceive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为「玩」，illudere 意为「玩弄某人」，也就是欺骗。

items.example: The prefix marks the play as directed at someone.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示把戏是冲着某人去的。

items.example: Ludere is the play root of the word family.
items.exampleCN: ludere 是这个词族的「玩」词根。

items.example: Illudere gives the verb of deceiving.
items.exampleCN: illudere 提供「欺骗」的动词义。

items.example: The suffix -io turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -io 把动词变成名词。

items.example: Illusion keeps the Latin noun meaning.
items.exampleCN: illusion 保留了拉丁语名词的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms illusory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 illusory。

items.example: The prefix dis- forms disillusion.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 构成 disillusion。

items.example: Disillusion means to take the illusion away.
items.exampleCN: disillusion 就是把 illusion 拿走。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms illusionist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 illusionist。

items.example: Illusionist names the stage performer.
items.exampleCN: illusionist 指舞台上的表演者。

definition_zh: 可想象的；想象得到的；能想见的
definition_en: able to be imagined, or as great or bad as it is possible to think of
core_image: 一个人闭着眼在空气里描画轮廓，指尖划过之处竟真的浮现出图形
scene: 设计师对着空荡荡的展馆，闭眼在空中比划了好一会儿。The empty hall was full of imaginable layouts, but none felt right.
sceneCN: 这里 imaginable 是「可想象的」（第 1 个义项：能够在头脑中构想出来的）；句意：空荡的展厅里满是想象得到的布置方案，却都不称心。它描摹的正是核心画面：在空处用想象勾出轮廓。

derivatives.zh: 由 imagine 加后缀 -ation 构成，义为「想象力；想象」
由 imagine 加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「富有想象力的」
由 imagine 加后缀 -ary 构成，义为「想象中的；虚构的」
由 imaginable 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可想象地」
动词词根，义为「想象；设想」

senses.title: Possible to picture in the mind
senses.definition: possible for a person to picture or conceive in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 能够在心里构想或描绘出来的
senses.example: Every imaginable shade of blue filled the sky at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时，天空中染满了可以想象到的每一种蓝色。
senses.why: The Latin root imago is a picture, and the suffix -able marks what can be done, so imaginable is what can be made into a picture in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 imago 意为「像、画面」，后缀 -able 表示「可以……的」，所以 imaginable 就是「能在心里构成画面」的。

senses.title: As great or bad as one can think of
senses.definition: used after a noun or with the best or worst to mean the greatest or worst one can think of
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，或与 the best、the worst 连用，表示能想到的最大或最坏的程度
senses.example: Prices rose faster than in any imaginable scenario.
senses.exampleCN: 价格上涨的速度超过任何可以想象的局面。
senses.why: If you can picture it, it belongs among the possibilities, so imaginable becomes a way of saying the extreme end of what could exist.
senses.whyCN: 只要能在心里画出画面，它就属于可能范围，imaginable 于是成了「可能存在的极限」的说法。

senses.title: Conceivable but unlikely to happen
senses.titleCN: 设想得到但未必真实的
senses.definition: possible in thought, even if there is no good reason to expect it
senses.definitionCN: 在思维上说得通，即便没有理由认为它真会发生
senses.example: It is barely imaginable that the wall could fall by itself.
senses.exampleCN: 那堵墙自己倒塌几乎是不可想象的。
senses.why: The suffix says only that the mind can form the picture, not that reality will match it, which is why the word so often appears in negatives.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀只说明头脑能构成画面，并不说明现实会照此发生，所以这个词常出现在否定句中。

intro.en: Imaginable joins imagine, from Latin imaginari, to picture, with the Latin and French suffix -able, meaning that can be.
intro.cn: imaginable 由 imagine（源自拉丁语 imaginari「在心里成像」）加拉丁语与法语后缀 -able（「可以……的」）构成。

items.en: Imago means an image or likeness, and imaginari means to picture something in the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 意为「像、图像」，动词 imaginari 意为「在心里想象」。

items.en: The suffix -abilis marks what is possible to do, the model for English -able.
items.cn: 拉丁语后缀 -abilis 表示「可……的」，是英语 -able 的来源模型。

items.en: French develops imagine and the ending -able on the same pattern.
items.cn: 古法语按同样的模式发展出 imagine 与词尾 -able。

items.en: Imaginable appears in English as a learned word beside imagination.
items.cn: 十四世纪 imaginable 作为学术用词与 imagination 一同出现在英语中。

items.en: The pattern the best imaginable and the worst imaginable becomes common in newspapers.
items.cn: 「the best imaginable」与「the worst imaginable」这类结构在十八世纪报刊中流行起来。

items.en: The adjective keeps both its neutral sense of possible to picture and its extreme sense at once.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个形容词同时保留「可以想象」的中性义与「程度到极限」的加强义。

note.en: Imaginable shares the Latin imago, picture, root with imagination and imaginative, and is easily confused with imaginary and imaginative.
note.cn: imaginable 与 imagination、imaginative 共享拉丁语 imago「图像」词根，又容易与一批拼写相近的词混淆。

entries.definition: existing only in the imagination
entries.definitionCN: 想象的；虚构的（并非「可想象的」）

entries.definition: good at creating new ideas
the ability to form pictures in the mind
in a way that can be pictured
possible to think about
able to be considered possible
able to happen or to be done
too great or too strange to picture

normalIntro.en: Imaginable is imagine plus -able: anything the mind can render as a picture becomes imaginable.
normalIntro.cn: imaginable 就是 imagine 加 -able：凡是头脑能画成图的东西，都是 imaginable。

normal.en: Imaginable ends in -able, so it means can be imagined, not made up.
normal.cn: imaginable 以 -able 结尾，意思是「能够被想象」，而不是「虚构出来的」。

normal.en: Imaginary means made up, imaginative means good at new ideas, and imaginable means possible to picture.
normal.cn: imaginary 是「虚构的」，imaginative 是「有想象力的」，imaginable 是「可以想象的」。

normal.en: The best imaginable is a set phrase for the finest thing one could picture.
normal.cn: the best imaginable 是固定搭配，指想象中得到的最好程度。

normal.en: Latin imago, a picture, is the root that imagination also keeps.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 imago「图像」是 imagination 同样保留的词根。

normal.en: Imaginable is rarely used in comparisons, and more imaginable is the usual form.
normal.cn: imaginable 很少直接加 -er，比较时通常说 more imaginable。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tracing an outline in empty air, and the shape appears wherever the finger passes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在空气里描画轮廓，指尖划过之处真的浮现出图形。

abstract.en: Think of a large blank card with a single frame drawn on it, waiting for the picture to be filled in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张大白卡片只画了一个相框，等着把画面填进去。

abstract.en: Imagine a dark room being scanned by torchlight, showing only what the beam can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一束手电光扫过暗室，只照见光能抵达的地方。

examples.en: The hotel offered every imaginable comfort.
examples.cn: 那家旅馆提供了一切能够想到的舒适设施。

examples.en: Conditions in the camp were the worst imaginable.
examples.cn: 营地的条件糟糕到了无法想象的地步。

examples.en: It is hardly imaginable that the two sides will ever agree.
examples.cn: 双方最终达成一致几乎是不可想象的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「想象麻吉能报」——脑子里能不能报出这个画面，就是它值不值得想；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 imago「图像」→ imaginari（在心里成像）→ 古法语 imaginer → 英语 imagine；再加拉丁语 -abilis（可……的）后的 -able，构成 imaginable，核心义「能被画进心里」。

sensesIntro.en: Imaginable starts with what the mind can picture, then turns into a measure of the utmost, and finally into a cautious word about what thought allows but reality may not.
sensesIntro.cn: imaginable 先指头脑能画出画面的东西，再引申为用来衡量极限的说法，最后成为表示「想得到但未必真会如此」的谨慎用词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand draws in the air and the outline appears wherever the finger passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在空中描画，指尖经过的地方就浮现出轮廓。

branches.en: Whatever the mind can turn into a picture is imaginable.
branches.cn: 头脑能转成画面的东西，都是可想象的。

branches.en: The same reach of mind measures the biggest or worst extreme.
branches.cn: 同一个思维范围也用来衡量最大或最坏的极限。

branches.en: Being picturable does not mean it will happen, hence the hesitant tone.
branches.cn: 「能画得出」不等于「会发生」，因此带有迟疑语气。

branches.en: Every imaginable choice and the best imaginable comfort draw on the same picture-making power.
branches.cn: 每种能想到的选项与能想到的最舒适，都来自同一种造画面的能力。

branches.en: The worst imaginable and it is hardly imaginable both push the able ending to its limit.
branches.cn: 最糟的能想到的情况与「几乎不可想象」，都把「能」字推到了边界。

intro.en: Imaginable is the imago, picture, root plus the Latin and French suffix -able; the family adds imagination, imaginative, imaginary, and imaginably.
intro.cn: imaginable 是词根 imago「图像」加拉丁语与法语后缀 -able 的产物；同一词族还有 imagination、imaginative、imaginary 与 imaginably。

latinIntro.en: Latin imago means a picture or a likeness, and imaginari means to form such a picture in the mind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imago 意为「图像、相似之物」，imaginari 意为「在心里构成这样的图像」。

items.example: The root imagin- comes from the Latin word for a picture.
items.exampleCN: 词根 imagin- 来自拉丁语中表示图像的那个词。

items.example: Imago is the direct root of the family.
items.exampleCN: imago 是这个词族的直接词根。

items.example: Imaginari supplies both the verb and the ability.
items.exampleCN: imaginari 同时提供动作与能力两个含义。

items.meaning: to form a picture in the mind
items.example: Imagine is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: imagine 是整个词族的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms imaginable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 imaginable。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms imagination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 imagination。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms imaginative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 imaginative。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms imaginary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 imaginary。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unimaginable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unimaginable。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms imaginably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 imaginably。

definition_zh: 不成熟的；幼稚的；未长成的；未发育完全的
definition_en: not yet fully grown, developed, or behaving in a sensible adult way
core_image: 一棵枝干还很柔弱的小树，果子又小又青，还挂在枝头
scene: 果园里，一筐果子按成熟程度分开摆放。The picking crew left the immature fruit on the tree for another month.
sceneCN: 这里 immature 指「未长成的」（第 3 个义项：动植物或果实尚未发育完全）；句意：采摘队把未成熟的果子留在树上，再多等一个月。

pos.zh: 不成熟的；幼稚的；未长成的

derivatives.zh: 由 immature 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为不成熟、幼稚
去掉否定前缀 im-，义为成熟、到期
由 mature 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为成熟地

senses.title: Fruit That Is Not Ready
senses.definition: not yet ready to eat, as fruit or crops that are still developing
senses.definitionCN: 果实或庄稼尚未发育到可以食用或收获的程度
senses.example: These pears are still immature and far too hard to eat.
senses.exampleCN: 这些梨还没成熟，硬得根本吃不了。
senses.why: The prefix im- means not, and mature comes from Latin maturus, meaning ripe in due time, so immature is the state of not being ripe yet.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 im- 表示「不」，而 mature 出自拉丁语 maturus，意为按时成熟，所以 immature 就是还没到成熟的时节。

senses.title: Not Fully Grown
senses.definition: not yet fully developed in body or mind, used of young people or animals
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心智尚未完全发育，用于人或动物
senses.example: The bird is immature and still has a dull brown coat.
senses.exampleCN: 这只鸟还没长大，羽毛还是暗淡的棕色。
senses.why: The botanical idea of the unripe fruit stretches to living things that have not yet reached their full size.
senses.whyCN: 果实未熟这一植物学意象延伸到尚未长到十足身量的生物，就得到「年幼的」这一义项。

senses.title: Not Fully Formed
senses.definition: not yet fully formed or at the right stage for its purpose
senses.definitionCN: 尚未完全成形，或还没有达到应有的阶段
senses.example: Immature seeds are lighter and float in water.
senses.exampleCN: 未发育完全的种子更轻，会浮在水面上。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original image of a fruit that is not ready and applies it to any half-formed product.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留果子尚未长好的原初意象，并把它用到任何只成形一半的东西上。

senses.title: Emotionally Childish
senses.definition: behaving in a way that is less sensible than is expected of an adult
senses.definitionCN: 行为表现得不够理智，不像一个成年人应有的样子
senses.example: It was immature of him to walk out in the middle of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他会议开到一半就甩门走人，太幼稚了。
senses.why: The image of the unripe fruit moves to behaviour that has not yet ripened into adult judgement.
senses.whyCN: 未熟果子的意象被移到人的行为上，指那种还没成熟到成年人判断力的表现。

senses.title: Not Ripe Yet
senses.definition: not fully ripe, describing plans, ideas, or works in progress
senses.definitionCN: 计划、想法或作品尚未完全成形、还处在发展之中
senses.example: The plan is still immature and needs a lot more work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划还不成熟，需要做大量补充。
senses.why: Anything still ripening on the tree can be described as immature, so the sense covers plans that are not ready to be put into action.
senses.whyCN: 还在树上成熟的果实都可以说 immature，于是这一义项也覆盖尚未准备好付诸实施的计划。

intro.en: Immature combines the negative prefix im-, a form of in-, with mature, which came from Latin maturus, meaning ripe or in due time.
intro.cn: immature 由否定前缀 im-（in- 的变体）与 mature 组成，后者出自拉丁语 maturus，意为「成熟、合时」。

items.en: Maturus describes fruit that is ripe in season and ready to be gathered.
items.cn: maturus 形容果子应时成熟、可以收获了。

items.en: Maturescere is the verb for growing ripe, and maturitas is ripeness itself.
items.cn: maturescere 是表示「成熟」的动词，maturitas 则是表示「成熟」的名词。

items.en: Matur is used for things that are ripe or ready, and enters Middle English in this form.
items.cn: matur 用来形容成熟或就绪的事物，并以此形式进入中古英语。

items.en: Mature becomes the English adjective for ripe, complete, and adult.
items.cn: mature 成为英语中表示成熟、完备、成年的形容词。

items.en: immature is built with im- in place of in- and extends from unripe fruit to childish behaviour.
items.cn: immature 把 in- 换成 im- 来构词，并从未熟的果子延伸到幼稚的行为。

note.en: Immature is the negative partner of mature, close to the mature family and to adjectives that describe a lack of grown-up judgement.
note.cn: immature 是 mature 的否定伙伴，与 mature 词族相邻，也与表示「不够成熟」的形容词相近。

entries.definition: the state of not being fully grown or developed
fully developed or behaving like an adult
happening too early, before the usual time
silly in a way that suits a child rather than an adult
entries.definitionCN: 幼稚的；孩子气的（含贬义）

entries.definition: lacking experience of the world and too trusting
young, or suited to young people

normalIntro.en: Immature is mature with the negative prefix im-, so every phrase reminds you that something has not ripened yet.
normalIntro.cn: immature 就是 mature 加否定前缀 im-，所以见到它就应该想到「还没长熟」。

normal.en: Immature is mature plus im-, the negative prefix, so immature is plainly not yet mature.
normal.cn: immature 等于 mature 加否定前缀 im-，意思就是「还不成熟」。

normal.en: Latin maturus meant ripe in due time, so an immature fruit is one that has missed its season so far.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 maturus 意为按时成熟，所以未熟的果子就是还没赶上时令的果子。

normal.en: The noun immaturity drops the final e of mature and adds -ity.
normal.cn: 名词 immaturity 去掉 mature 末尾的 e 再加 -ity。

normal.en: Emotionally immature describes someone who sulks or gives up when things go wrong.
normal.cn: emotionally immature 描述那种一遇挫折就闹脾气或甩手不干的人。

normal.en: In biology, an immature bird or insect has not yet reached its fully grown form.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，immature bird 或 immature insect 指的是还没长成成体的鸟或昆虫。

abstract.en: Picture a green peach still hard on the branch while the ripe ones fill the basket.
abstract.cn: 想象一只又青又硬的桃还挂在枝头，成熟的果子已经装满篮子。

abstract.en: Think of a chick with fluffy feathers that cannot use its wings yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一只长着绒毛、翅膀还飞不起来的小鸟。

abstract.en: Imagine a small green seed that has not filled out into a kernel.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒还干瘪发绿、尚未饱满的种子。

examples.en: The shop does not sell immature fruit because it is too sour.
examples.cn: 这家店不卖没熟透的水果，因为太酸了。

examples.en: Her immature jokes annoyed everyone at the dinner table.
examples.cn: 她那些幼稚的笑话让满桌人都很扫兴。

examples.en: The plan was still immature and needed a great deal of revision.
examples.cn: 这个计划还不成熟，需要大幅修改。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一妈球」——像一只又青又硬的小球，还没长熟；这只是读音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 maturus（成熟、合时）→ 英语 mature（成熟的）+ 否定前缀 im-（= in-，不）→ immature（不成熟的；未长成的），核心义「还没长熟」。

sensesIntro.en: Immature starts with fruit that is not ripe, moves to living things that are not fully grown, and then to behaviour and plans that have not ripened into adult judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: immature 从未熟的果子出发，先指尚未长成的生物，再移到还没有成熟到成年人判断力的行为和计划上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small green fruit still hanging on the branch, hard and not yet ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗又小又青的果子还挂在枝头，硬邦邦的，还不到采摘的时候。

branches.en: Unripe fruit is the most concrete sense and the source of the image.
branches.cn: 未熟的果子是最具体的义项，也是整个意象的源头。

branches.en: Living things not yet full-grown sit one step away from the unripe fruit.
branches.cn: 尚未长大的生物离未熟的果子只有一步之遥。

branches.en: Anything still forming keeps the botanical idea of something not ready.
branches.cn: 任何还在成形中的事物都保留了「尚未长好」的植物学意念。

branches.en: Childish behaviour is the human sense, where judgement has not ripened.
branches.cn: 幼稚的行为是人的层面，指判断力还没长熟。

branches.en: A plan and a piece of fruit are both described as immature when they are not ready to be used.
branches.cn: 当计划和果实都不能派上用场时，都可以用 immature 来形容。

intro.en: immature is built from the Latin adjective maturus with the negative prefix im-, and its family includes the nouns immaturity and maturity.
intro.cn: immature 由拉丁语形容词 maturus 加否定前缀 im- 构成，同族词有名词 immaturity 与 maturity。

latinIntro.en: Latin maturus means ripe in season, and the verb maturescere means to grow ripe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 maturus 意为应时成熟的，动词 maturescere 意为成熟。

items.example: The prefix im- turns mature into its negative.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 把 mature 变成否定词。

items.example: Mature is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: mature 是基础形容词。

items.example: Immature adds the negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: immature 加了否定前缀。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms immaturity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 immaturity。

items.example: Immaturity names the state of not being ripe.
items.exampleCN: immaturity 指未成熟的状态。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或状态的词尾
items.example: Latin maturitas and English mature trace back through this ending.
items.exampleCN: mature 的形态经由拉丁词尾演变而来。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms maturely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 maturely。

items.example: The prefix pre- adds the idea of early.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 加上「早」的意思。

items.example: Mature forms matureness in rare use.
items.exampleCN: mature 偶与 -ness 构成 matureness。

definition_zh: 无法衡量的；无穷无尽的；浩瀚的；不可估量的
definition_en: too large or too great to be measured, counted, or fully judged
core_image: 一片望不到边的星空，没有任何尺子能量到它的尽头
scene: 孩子站在山顶上，抬头看整片星空。The night sky over the desert felt immeasurable.
sceneCN: 这里 immeasurable 指「浩瀚无边的」（第 2 个义项：空间大到无法丈量）；句意：沙漠上方的夜空让人觉得浩瀚无边。

pos.zh: 无法衡量的；无穷无尽的

derivatives.zh: 由 immeasurable 加副词后缀 -ably 构成，义为无法衡量地、极其
去掉否定前缀 im-，义为可测量的
词根词，义为测量；量度

senses.title: Too Large to Measure
senses.titleCN: 无法衡量的；不可估量的
senses.definition: far too great in amount or degree to be measured
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上太大，无法测量
senses.example: The project brought immeasurable benefits to the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目给整个村子带来了无法估量的好处。
senses.why: The prefix im- means not and measurable means able to be measured, so the word literally names what the ruler cannot reach.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 im- 表示「不」，measurable 意为「可测量的」，所以这个词字面上就是尺子够不到的东西。

senses.title: Without Limits
senses.definition: having no visible limit in space or extent
senses.definitionCN: 在空间或范围上看不到边界
senses.example: The immeasurable wastes of ice stretched to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 无边无际的冰原一直延伸到地平线。
senses.why: Once something cannot be measured, it is easy to picture it as stretching beyond any edge, which gives the sense of vast space.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦无法丈量，就很容易被想象成超出任何边界，于是产生「浩瀚无边」的义项。

senses.title: Beyond Words
senses.definition: greater than words can express, as of feelings or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 比语言所能表达的还要大，用于情感或品质
senses.example: She feels immeasurable gratitude to the nurse who saved her son.
senses.exampleCN: 她对救了自己儿子的护士心怀难以言尽的感激。
senses.why: Feelings cannot be put on a scale, so the idea of the unmeasurable naturally turns into the idea of what words cannot contain.
senses.whyCN: 情感无法放在秤上量，所以「无法衡量」的意念自然转成了「言语装不下」的义项。

senses.title: A Vast Period
senses.definition: extending over a period of time too long to be counted
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上延续得太久，长得数不清
senses.example: After an immeasurable pause, he finally spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长得难以计量的停顿之后，他终于开口了。
senses.why: Time too is something we measure with clocks, so a span that clocks cannot count becomes immeasurable.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是我们用钟表来测的东西，所以连钟表都数不完的时段就成了 immeasurable。

intro.en: Immeasurable is im- plus measurable, and measurable comes from measure, which entered English from Old French mesure and Latin mensura.
intro.cn: immeasurable 是 im- 加 measurable，而 measurable 出自 measure；measure 经古法语 mesure 来自拉丁语 mensura。

items.en: Mensura means a measuring or a measure, from the verb metiri, to measure.
items.cn: mensura 意为量度、尺度，出自动词 metiri（测量）。

items.en: Im- is the form that the negative prefix in- takes before m, as in immensus, meaning unmeasured.
items.cn: im- 是否定前缀 in- 在 m 前的变体，拉丁语 immensus 即「未测量的」。

items.en: Mesure passes the measuring word into French and then into English.
items.cn: mesure 把表示测量的词带进法语，再进入英语。

items.en: Measure appears in English with the senses of size, amount, and the act of measuring.
items.cn: measure 在英语中出现，义为尺寸、数量与测量的行为。

items.en: Measurable adds -able, and immeasurable adds the negative prefix to name what no scale can hold.
items.cn: measurable 加后缀 -able，immeasurable 再加否定前缀，用来指秤和尺都装不下的东西。

note.en: Immeasurable belongs to the measure family and sits close to adjectives for things too big to be counted.
note.cn: immeasurable 属于 measure 词族，与那些表示「大到数不清」的形容词相邻。

entries.definition: to find the size or amount of something
able to be measured
to a degree that cannot be measured
without any limit or end
having no limits at all
too great to be calculated
entries.definitionCN: 不可估量的；难以计算的

normalIntro.en: Immeasurable is measurable with a negative prefix, so the whole family turns around the idea of measuring.
normalIntro.cn: immeasurable 就是 measurable 加否定前缀，整个词族都围绕「测量」这个动作。

normal.en: Immeasurable is measurable plus im-, so the word announces that no measuring is possible.
normal.cn: immeasurable 是 measurable 加否定前缀 im-，直接说明「量不出来」。

normal.en: The stem is measure, which also gives measurement, measurable, and measurably.
normal.cn: 词干是 measure，由此还派生 measurement、measurable、measurably。

normal.en: Immeasurable is always an adjective before a noun, as in immeasurable value or immeasurable joy.
normal.cn: immeasurable 总是形容词，放在名词前，如 immeasurable value 或 immeasurable joy。

normal.en: The adverb immeasurably often means very much, as in immeasurably better.
normal.cn: 副词 immeasurably 常表示「无比地」，如 immeasurably better。

normal.en: Latin immensus, unmeasured, is the same idea built in Latin with the same negative prefix.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 immensus 意为「未测量的」，用同样的否定前缀表达了同一意念。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler stretching out and never reaching the far edge of the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子一路伸出去，却永远够不到天空的边缘。

abstract.en: Think of a sea so wide that no boat can cross it in a lifetime.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海宽得没有任何船能在一生中横渡。

abstract.en: Imagine thanking a nurse so much that no number of words is enough.
abstract.cn: 想象想向护士道谢，却发现多少话都说不完。

examples.en: Clean water has immeasurable value for public health.
examples.cn: 清洁的水对公共卫生有不可估量的价值。

examples.en: Her patience made an immeasurable difference to the team.
examples.cn: 她的耐心给团队带来了难以衡量的改变。

examples.en: Beyond the last houses lay immeasurable fields of wheat.
examples.cn: 最后几户人家的房屋之外，是一望无际的麦田。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一没辙拉」——拿尺子去量，实在没辙，拉都拉不到头；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 metiri（测量）→ mensura（量度）→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure → measurable（可测量的）+ 否定前缀 im-（不）→ immeasurable（无法衡量的），核心义「量不出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Immeasurable begins with amounts too great for any scale, then spreads to vast space, to feelings beyond words, and to time too long to count.
sensesIntro.cn: immeasurable 先指大到任何秤都称不了的量，再扩到浩瀚的空间、言说不尽的情感，以及长得数不过来的时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler reaching out into the night sky and finding no edge to stop at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子伸向夜空，怎么也找不到可以停下的边界。

branches.en: The most direct sense names an amount that no scale can hold.
branches.cn: 最直接的义项指任何一种秤都称不出的量。

branches.en: Unmeasurable size turns into the feeling of endless space.
branches.cn: 无法丈量的尺寸变成了空间无边的感受。

branches.en: Feelings cannot be weighed, so they become the things words cannot carry.
branches.cn: 情感称不出重量，于是成为言语装不下的东西。

branches.en: Clock time is unmeasurable when the span is too long to count.
branches.cn: 当时段长得数不过来时，钟表就失去了丈量的意义。

branches.en: Both an immeasurable benefit and immeasurable gratitude are things we can feel but never put a number to.
branches.cn: 无法估量的益处与无穷的感激都是能感受到却给不出数字的东西。

intro.en: immeasurable is formed inside English from measure with the suffix -able and the negative prefix im-, and its Latin twin is immensus.
intro.cn: immeasurable 是英语内部用 measure 加后缀 -able 与否定前缀 im- 构成的，它在拉丁语中的对应形式是 immensus。

latinIntro.en: Latin metiri means to measure, mensura means a measure, and immensus means unmeasured.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，mensura 意为量度，immensus 意为未测量的。

items.example: The prefix im- sits before the letter m in immeasurable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 在 immeasurable 里位于字母 m 之前。

items.meaning: to find the size or amount
items.example: Measure is the living stem of the family.
items.exampleCN: measure 是整个词族的活词干。

items.example: The suffix -able forms measurable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 measurable。

items.example: Measurable is the positive form.
items.exampleCN: measurable 是肯定形式。

items.example: Immeasurable is the negative form.
items.exampleCN: immeasurable 是否定形式。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms measurably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 measurably。

items.meaning: to a degree that cannot be measured
items.example: Immeasurably adds both the prefix and the adverb ending.
items.exampleCN: immeasurably 同时加了前缀与副词词尾。

items.meaning: the act or result of measuring
items.example: The suffix -ment forms measurement.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 measurement。

definition_en: to put something completely under a liquid, or to keep yourself fully involved in an activity
core_image: 整个人沉进水里，四周全是同一片蓝
scene: 厨房的洗菜池里，妈妈把一把青菜按进水里。She immersed the vegetables in cold water to wash off the soil.
sceneCN: 这里 immerse 指「浸没」（第 2 个义项：把东西完全放进液体里）；句意：她把蔬菜浸在冷水里，冲掉泥土。

senses.title: To Put Under Liquid
senses.definition: to put something or someone completely under a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 把某物或某人完全放入液体之中
senses.example: Immerse the cloth in warm water for a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 把布浸在温水里几分钟。
senses.why: The Latin mers- means to dip or sink, so the core picture is a thing sinking right under the surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mers- 意为「浸入、下沉」，所以核心画面是物体整个沉到液面之下。

senses.title: To Sink into a Medium
senses.definition: to let something become completely surrounded by a substance, light, or sound
senses.definitionCN: 让某物被某种物质、光线或声音完全包围
senses.example: The room was immersed in a soft golden light.
senses.exampleCN: 房间沐浴在柔和的金色光线里。
senses.why: Anything that surrounds a body like liquid can be the medium it sinks into, so light and sound take the place of water.
senses.whyCN: 任何像液体一样包住身体的介质，都可以成为下沉的所在，于是水换成了光和声音。

senses.title: To Absorb Someone Deeply
senses.definition: to involve someone so completely that nothing else is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 使人完全投入其中，以至于注意不到其他事情
senses.example: The story immersed him so deeply that he missed his stop.
senses.exampleCN: 故事让他太投入了，连该下车的站都错过了。
senses.why: Being under water means the outside world goes quiet and muffled, which is exactly how full involvement feels.
senses.whyCN: 沉在水下意味着外面的世界变得安静而模糊，这正是全身心投入的感受。

senses.title: To Absorb Oneself in Study
senses.definition: to spend all your attention on a subject or activity
senses.definitionCN: 把全部注意力放在某个主题或活动上
senses.example: She immersed herself in local history for the whole summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她整个夏天都潜心研究当地历史。
senses.why: The pattern immerse oneself in keeps the image of sinking and applies it to study: the learner goes all the way in.
senses.whyCN: immerse oneself in 这一结构保留了「下沉」的意象，并用到学习上：学习者一直沉到底。

senses.title: To Reach Every Part
senses.definition: to fill or soak something completely through
senses.definitionCN: 把某物里里外外都浸透、充满
senses.example: The old document was immersed in glue before it was pressed flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这份旧文件在被压平之前先浸透了胶水。
senses.why: If something stays long enough under a liquid, the liquid reaches every part, which adds the sense of soaking all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 东西在液体里泡得够久，液体就会到达每一处，这就增添了「浸透到底」的义项。

intro.en: Immerse comes from Latin immersus, the past participle of immergere, which joins in-, meaning into, with mergere, meaning to dip or sink.
intro.cn: immerse 出自拉丁语 immergere 的过去分词 immersus，其中 in- 表示「进入」，mergere 表示「浸入、下沉」。

items.en: Mergere means to dip, plunge, or sink something into liquid.
items.cn: mergere 意为把东西浸入、投入液体中。

items.en: Immergere adds in- into that verb to mean plunge into.
items.cn: immergere 在前者上加 in-（进入），意为「使沉入」。

items.en: Immersus is the past participle, and the adjective immersus describes something sunk.
items.cn: immersus 是过去分词，形容词 immersus 描述已经沉入水中的东西。

items.en: English borrows immerse mainly through Latin and French forms meaning to plunge into water.
items.cn: 英语主要通过拉丁语和法语形式借入 immerse，义为「投入水中」。

items.en: Immersion and immersive extend the word to language teaching and computer games.
items.cn: immersion 与 immersive 把这个词延伸到语言教学与电子游戏。

note.en: Immerse belongs to the merge family and sits close to verbs about sinking into water or into an activity.
note.cn: immerse 属于 merg 词族，与「沉入水中」或「投入活动」的动词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Immerse turns around the Latin verb mergere, to sink, paired with the prefix in- into, so every form keeps the picture of going down into something.
normalIntro.cn: immerse 围绕拉丁语动词 mergere（下沉）与前缀 in-（进入）展开，各种形式都保留「沉下去」的画面。

normal.en: Immerse joins the prefix im- with the root merg-, which you also see in submerge and emerge.
normal.cn: immerse 用前缀 im- 加词根 merg-，submerge 与 emerge 里也能看到这个词根。

normal.en: The noun is immersion, and the adjective is immersive, as in an immersive game.
normal.cn: 名词是 immersion，形容词是 immersive，如 an immersive game。

normal.en: The main pattern is immerse something in something, or immerse oneself in an activity.
normal.cn: 主要结构是 immerse something in something，或 immerse oneself in 某种活动。

normal.en: Be immersed in means to be deeply involved, as in she was immersed in her work.
normal.cn: be immersed in 表示深陷其中，如「她埋头工作」就可以用它来表达。

normal.en: Family words built on the same root include submerge and emerge.
normal.cn: 同一词根构成的同族词有 submerge 与 emerge。

abstract.en: Picture yourself stepping down into a warm bath until the water covers your shoulders.
abstract.cn: 想象自己走进一池温水，一直沉到水没过肩膀。

abstract.en: Think of the noise of the city fading away as you go under the surface.
abstract.cn: 想象沉到水面之下时，城市的噪声一点点消失。

abstract.en: Imagine reading a novel so deeply that you do not hear your own name.
abstract.cn: 想象读一本小说读得入神，连别人叫你名字都没听见。

examples.en: Immerse the tea leaves in hot water for three minutes.
examples.cn: 把茶叶浸泡在热水里三分钟。

examples.en: She was so immersed in the game that she forgot lunch.
examples.cn: 她太投入游戏，把午饭都忘了。

examples.en: The museum immerses visitors in the daily life of ancient merchants.
examples.cn: 博物馆让参观者沉浸在古代商人的日常生活里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一莫失」——人一沉进水里，就「莫失」了自己；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 mergere（浸入、下沉）→ immergere（使沉入）→ 过去分词 immersus → 英语 immerse，核心义「整个沉进去」。

sensesIntro.en: Immerse starts with a body going under liquid, then stretches to light and sound that surround you, and finally to attention that sinks so deep that everything else disappears.
sensesIntro.cn: immerse 从身体沉入液体开始，扩展到包围你的光与声音，最后指注意力沉得深到让其他一切都消失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole body going down under the surface until the water closes over it.
core.cn: 核心意象：整个人沉到水面之下，水在头顶合拢。

branches.en: The physical sense of putting a thing into liquid is the root of everything else.
branches.cn: 把东西放进液体里的物理义项是其他一切义项的根。

branches.en: Anything that surrounds like liquid can be the medium: light, sound, or weather.
branches.cn: 任何像液体一样包围事物的介质都可以充当它：光线、声音或天气。

branches.en: A muffled underwater world becomes the image of complete attention.
branches.cn: 水下沉闷安静的世界变成了完全专注的意象。

branches.en: Studying with no distraction is the everyday sense of immerging oneself in a subject.
branches.cn: 心无旁骛地学习就是 immerse oneself in 某门学问的日常义项。

branches.en: Long soaking and total involvement share the idea of liquid reaching every part.
branches.cn: 长时间浸泡与全身心投入共有「液体遍及每一处」的意念。

definition_en: the act of putting something completely into a liquid, or the state of being deeply involved in an activity or environment

scene: 学语言的学生被安排在说外语的家庭里同吃同住。Students in the programme learn French through total immersion, living and eating with French-speaking host families.

senses.title: The act of plunging something into liquid
senses.definition: the action of putting something completely into a liquid so that it is covered
senses.definitionCN: 把某物完全放入液体中，使其被液体盖住的动作
senses.example: Full immersion in cold water cools the metal quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 完全浸入冷水中能让金属迅速冷却。
senses.why: The Latin base mersus means dipped, and the prefix in- means into, so immersion is literally a dipping into water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 mersus 意为「被浸入的」，前缀 in- 表示「进入」，所以 immersion 字面就是「浸入水中」，核心意象是一只整个没入水中的手或物。

senses.title: Deep involvement in an activity or environment
senses.definition: a state of being so involved in something that you lose awareness of everything else
senses.definitionCN: 对某事投入之深，以致忘掉周围一切的状态
senses.example: Her daily immersion in baroque music shaped her taste.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天沉浸在巴洛克音乐中，塑造了自己的品味。
senses.why: The watery image turns mental, as being surrounded by a task or a world is like being covered by water.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人被一项任务或一个世界整个包住时，就像被水包住一样，「浸在水里」的意象于是转为「沉浸其中」，注意力被包得没有缝隙。

senses.title: A school programme in a second language
senses.definition: a teaching method in which lessons are given almost entirely in the target language
senses.definitionCN: 几乎完全使用目标语言授课的教学方式
senses.example: Immersion in a second language helps children speak it naturally.
senses.exampleCN: 第二语言的沉浸式学习能让孩子自然地开口说话。
senses.why: Learners are placed inside the language, so the older watery metaphor becomes the name of the method itself.
senses.whyCN: 把学习者整个放进目标语言里，就像把人放进水中，这个旧比喻后来干脆成了这种教学法本身的名字。

senses.title: Immersion in virtual or digital worlds
senses.definition: the effect of a game, film, or device that makes the user feel present inside the scene
senses.definitionCN: 游戏、影片或设备令使用者仿佛身在现场的效果
senses.example: A headset adds a sense of immersion to the game.
senses.exampleCN: 头戴设备让游戏多了一份身临其境的感觉。
senses.why: The user is placed inside the virtual scene and surrounded by it, exactly what water does to a body.
senses.whyCN: 使用者被放进了虚拟场景之中并被其包围，和身体被水包围的感觉完全相同，于是技术界借用了这个词。

senses.title: Immersion as a rite in baptism
senses.definition: the Christian rite of dipping a person completely in water
senses.definitionCN: 基督教把人完全浸入水中的洗礼仪式
senses.example: That church performs a full immersion of each new member.
senses.exampleCN: 那座教堂为每位新成员施行全身浸水礼。
senses.why: The earliest Christian baptism was a full dipping into a river, so the physical sense entered religious use first.
senses.whyCN: 早期基督教洗礼是在河里整个人下水，因此「浸没」这个物理义项最先进入宗教用法，并一直保留到今天。

intro.en: Immersion comes from Latin immersio, a dipping in, built on mergere, to dip.
intro.cn: immersion 来自拉丁语 immersio（浸入），词根为 mergere（浸没、下沉）。

items.en: The root meant to sink, traced in Latin mergere.
items.cn: 词根义为「下沉」，保存在拉丁语 mergere 中。

items.en: Mergere means to dip or sink, and its participle gives mersus.
items.cn: mergere 意为浸没、下沉，其分词形式为 mersus。

items.en: Immersion is the noun for a dipping in.
items.cn: immersion 是表示「浸入」的拉丁语名词。

items.en: The noun travels through church Latin into French writers.
items.cn: 这个名词经由教会拉丁语进入法语写作。

items.en: English uses it first for baptism and for dipping objects in liquid.
items.cn: 英语先用于洗礼与把物体浸入液体。

items.en: Later it extends to study, games, and virtual scenes.
items.cn: 其后又扩展到学习、游戏与虚拟场景。

note.en: Immersion is a Latin noun of dipping, close to immerse, emersion, and immersion in a task or language.
note.cn: immersion 是表示「浸入」的拉丁语名词，与 immerse、emersion 形近，与强调「专注」的说法意义相近。

normalIntro.en: Immersion is being inside water, and by extension inside a language, a task, or a virtual world.
normalIntro.cn: immersion 是整个人在水里，进而引申为身在一种语言、一项任务或一个虚拟世界里。

normal.en: Immerse is the verb, and immersion is the noun that follows it.
normal.cn: immerse 是动词，immersion 是由它而来的名词。

normal.en: In a total immersion course, the teacher refuses the first language.
normal.cn: 在 total immersion 课程里，老师拒绝使用母语。

normal.en: Immersion in a subject means thinking about it all day.
normal.cn: immersion in a subject 就是指一整天都在想这件事。

normal.cn: 词尾 -sion 标记动作名词，immersion 与 submersion 都是如此。

normal.cn: 对比 absorption：两者都表示被完全吸进去，但 immersion 保留了「水」的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a diver going under with no part of the body left dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一名潜水者整个没入水下，身上没有一处是干的。

abstract.en: Imagine an hour passing while you read without hearing anyone call you.
abstract.cn: 想象你读书读了一小时，却完全没听见有人喊你。

abstract.en: See a classroom where every child speaks only the new language.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室里，每个孩子都只用新语言说话。

examples.en: Immersion in cold water can be dangerous for young children.
examples.cn: 对幼童来说，整个浸入冷水可能很危险。

examples.en: Some parents choose language immersion schools for their children.
examples.cn: 一些家长为孩子选择语言沉浸式学校。

examples.en: The film creates a strong sense of immersion with its sound design.
examples.cn: 这部电影凭借声音设计营造出很强的沉浸感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一莫身」——一头莫（没）进身子里，水把整个人都没过了，就是浸没；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Immersion begins with the physical act of dipping, moves to being absorbed in an activity, then names a language programme, a virtual effect, and finally a baptism.

branches.en: Being surrounded by a task replaces water with attention.

branches.en: A language programme puts the learner inside the language.
branches.cn: 语言教学法把学习者整个放进目标语言里。

branches.en: A virtual world surrounds the senses in the same way water does.
branches.cn: 虚拟世界像水一样包围人的感官。

branches.en: Baptism keeps the literal image of a full dipping.
branches.cn: 洗礼保留了「整个人下水」的字面画面。
